newsitem.title: UK: Rolls Royce admits engine failures - paper.
newsitem.headline: Rolls Royce admits engine failures - paper.

text.p: UK aero-engine firm Rolls-Royce Plc may face compensation demands from airlines after admitting it will have to modify engines that have caused some in-flight shutdowns, the Financial Times reported.
Rolls-Royce said turbine blade failures had occured in a version of its RB211 engine that has been used since 1989 on Boeing 747s and 767s, the paper reported.
The FT quoted the company as saying none of the shutdowns posed a danger to passengers and it was not unusual for airlines to experience problems like this with engines from all manufacturers.
The company was not immediately available for comment.
The FT cited a report to be published on Tuesday in Flight International magazine which said the engine problems had already cost airlines $200 million in extra maintenance costs.
